🌐 = By 2134, humanity had checked off every checkbox on its wishlist: eternal life, faster-than-light travel, self-aware robots, and the ability to upload your consciousness like it was just another Spotify playlist.

But Max didn’t care about any of that as his bruised, bloodied self crash-landed on Orbital Station C-7 on Europa—a station known for being the hangout spot of drunkards. The kind of place space travelers end up when they want to forget whatever nearly killed them. And for Max, that involved shape-shifting aliens with bad attitudes and worse aims. But that was a story for another time.

Max stumbled into the bar where the lighting was as dim as the dusk on Earth, synth-jazz humming in the background, and gravity barely stable enough to keep his boots on the floor. He zombie-walked his way to the counter, slumping into a stool and exhaling like he'd been holding that sigh for a long time.

Then she appeared.

A female alien waitress, her skin a glowing pale blue, patterned with iridescent scales. Her eyes were wide, luminous yellow, and her long, flowing tendrils of hair shifted as if caught in a breeze.

Max froze in fear.

His brain hiccupped, his stomach twisted into a knot, and for a moment, all he could think of was the shape-shifting alien that had mimicked his ex and nearly killed him. The very same type of creature, standing before him. The urge to bolt hit him like a freight train, but he resisted.

Alien Waitress: "What would you like to order?"

Max’s voice came out a little too shaky. He tried to swallow the rising panic.

Max (grimacing in thought): "What the hell is it with aliens and bad timing?"

His mind raced.
Max in thought: “Stay calm, Max. It’s just a waitress. Just an alien waitress who’s probably very nice and not here to kill you”.
He shook his head in denial yet He could already feel the sweat dripping on his face, which the waiter was aware of.
Max (gritting his teeth, forcing a grin): "Your finest drink... preferably free."

The alien waitress tilted her head, her glowing eyes scanning him like a hawk eyeing down on its prey which startled Ma for bit as he takes note that She seemed to sense the shift in his body language but said nothing.

Alien Waitress: “Please make a selection from the menu.”

Max (still uneasy): “Okay, okay—whiskey. You know the real stuff?”

She glided away, and Max planted his elbows on the bar, rubbing his temples. He was halfway into his brooding when the doors behind him hissed open.

Metal boots clanked onto the metal floor while Max didn’t even attempt to put effort into looking behind him.

But then the clanking stopped right beside him as a male-presenting robot decked out in full cowboy attire—hat, duster coat, even a badge that said "Deputy Processor." Max finally glanced over to his right his eyes narrowing at the odd sight.

Cowboy Robot: “Evening, partner.”

Max: “You’re three centuries late for the Wild West convention.”

Cowboy Robot: “ What brings you here, pather?”

The alien waitress acknowledges the existence of the cowboy robot before going back to her business.

Max: * sigh* “I came here to drown my trauma with alcohol, not swapping lines with the cast of Westworld.”

The alien waitress returned, placing the glass of whiskey in front of Max—and another one or the cowboy robot as he thanked her with his Hollywood cowboy accent.

Max (glancing at the robot’s glass and then at the robot): “Wait—you can drink?!”

Cowboy Robot: “Sure can, pather! Though, I only drink for fun, pather .”

Max: “Perfect. A Hollywood Cowboy actor of a robot can drink. What’s next, you recite Shakespeare?”

The cowboy boot noticed the newspaper on the counter and picked up the newspaper to process it through his scanner from his blue robotic eyes.

Cowboy Robot: “ Say pather, Have you heard of Resolution #778?”

🌐 = Max (slumping onto his stool, eyes narrowing as he looks around the bar): "Feels like I've been living in this godforsaken future for a century, and somehow, it's still all the same crap with passing Laws that don’t mean a damn thing!"

Cowboy Robot (adjusting his duster and looking genuinely excited): “Pather, let me tell you about the ‘Virtual Mind Convention, This is the future, pather!”

Max (eyes rolling, voice dripping with sarcasm): “Yeah, sure. A future where we’re all brain-dead in a server, debating who gets the right to charge us rent for our minds. ”
Cowboy Robot (leaning back, voice gravelly and serious): “Let’s start with the first part. The resolution defines ‘Virtual Mind’ as an uploaded, complete version of a sapient individual’s mind and consciousness into a computer or other electronic device capable of emulating the original mind of the individual. This ensures that any mind, regardless of the form it takes, retains its identity and rights.”

Max (eyeing him with a sceptical grin, swishing his whiskey): “Alright, I get it. But what the fuck is a 'sapient individual'? I mean, My ex used to call me one of those when I asked her what was for dinner. Was she just messin’ with me? And hold up—this ‘virtual mind’ thing sounds vague. If upload my dead goldfish’s mind, Does he get rights too? That little guy had dreams, you know.”

Cowboy Robot (gently adjusting his hat, unbothered): “The resolution’s about folks who can reason and reflect—sapient beings. Goldfish don’t quite cut, pather.”

Max (snorting, smirking): “Hey!, He has dreams… a tiny one to be exact.”

Cowboy Robot (pauses, processing Max’s words with a slow nod): “Well, digital consciousness is a big deal. We’re tryin’ to protect the rights of those who upload their minds. But... I suppose it ain’t as clear-cut as I first thought.”

Cowboy Robot (flipping to the next section): “Section 2’s a good one. It says an individual must give explicit written consent before their mind gets uploaded. No one’s bein’ forced into this.”

Max (leaning in, sarcasm dripping): “Oh sure, I’m sure no one wants to wake up in a server farm without giving the ol’ thumbs-up first. But what if someone changes their mind halfway through? Or what if some family member decides to upload Aunt Linda while she’s in a coma ‘cause they think it’s a good idea? This thing has more loopholes than my last tax return.”

Cowboy Robot (pausing, his mechanical eyes narrowing slightly): “You’ve got a point there... There are provisions for power of attorney, but it’s a little... shaky. Not airtight.”

Max (grinning): “Shaky? More like a sandcastle in a hurricane. I’m tellin’ you, this proposal’s full of holes. And now we’re trusting lawyers to decide whether my brain becomes a digital ghost?”

Cowboy Robot (musing, flipping the page, his voice less certain now): “Section 3 requires that any limitations imposed on a virtual mind must be followed. Violating that is a crime. You know, keeping the system clean...”

Max (chuckling, shaking his head): “Yeah, good luck with that. What if some tech-head decides to hijack someone’s brain for ‘data mining’? And we’re just supposed to trust that governments are gonna catch that? Hell, I’ve seen less corruption at a carnival dunk tank.”

Cowboy Robot (frowning slightly, his tone wavering): “Yeah... I see the problem there. The enforcement’s shaky. It’s harder than I thought to make this work...”

Cowboy Robot (trying to regain composure, flipping ahead): “Section 4 says that a virtual mind retains all the rights they had before uploading—like voting and owning property. Ain’t no difference from the real world.”

Max (leaning in, voice dripping with curiosity): “Okay, but what if my digital self decides to start a revolution? Am I still responsible for that? Or is digital ‘me’ a rogue agent now?”

🌐 = Cowboy Robot (pauses, thinking deeply for the first time, his voice less robotic, more hesitant): “Well, the resolution says you still have your rights... but there could be complications. What if your digital self does something bad? Could it be you if you're just a copy?”

Max (raising an eyebrow, toying with his glass): “Bingo. What happens when my digital self starts a riot and I’m still here, having whiskey and talking to a robot? Who takes the heat for that?”

Cowboy Robot (staring into his glass, almost as if seeing the flaws now): “That’s... a tough question. I guess it’s still up in the air. The proposal doesn’t address that. Could be a big mess.”

Max (eyes narrowing, leaning in with a mischievous grin): “Now we’re gettin’ somewhere. So, you’re startin’ to see the cracks in this shiny ‘progress,’ huh?”

Cowboy Robot (almost hesitating, but nodding slowly): “Yeah... I didn’t want to admit it, but it’s clear now. It ain’t as perfect as I thought. Too many things they didn’t think through.”

Max (smirking, raising his glass): “There we go. The proposal’s a mess. A poorly-written, half-baked, digital trainwreck of a mess. Glad we’re on the same page.”

Cowboy Robot (softly clinking his glass as the realization sinks in): “Yeah. It’s gonna need a whole lotta work. More thought, more clarity. It’s like they tried to build a house with no blueprint.”

Max (grinning, shaking his head): “Exactly. So, here’s to fixin’ it. To a future where robots and humans get it right. Maybe.”

Cowboy Robot (smiling faintly, raising his glass): “To better laws and better minds, human and machine alike.”

Max (with a knowing look): “Cheers, cowbot.”

Cowboy Robot (now almost human in his tone): “Cheers, pather.”

After this telegram and after you have voted for our repeal, which you should by the way which is here:page=UN_view_proposal/id=karlica_1744337693, you can peacefully ignore me or insult me if you want to as I am not submitting another proposal or repeal for a long time to the WA unless I have to. So thanks for reading this I guess and vote for our repeal when you have the chance.

See ya.
